title: Starlette authentication

findings.title: requires decorator does not validate that auth exists before accessing conn.auth.scopes
findings.explanation: The wrapper functions (async_wrapper, sync_wrapper) assume request.auth is always present and has a scopes attribute. If a request reaches the wrapper without auth being initialized, an unhandled AttributeError propagates to the user, potentially leaking stack traces or causing 500 errors instead of a clean authentication failure.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard at the top of async_wrapper and sync_wrapper to check hasattr(request, 'auth') and that request.auth is not None before checking scopes. If auth is missing, treat as unauthorized (raise HTTPException or redirect as configured).
findings.suggested_test: Create a request mock without auth and verify requires([]) raises HTTPException(403) rather than AttributeError.

findings.title: has_required_scope does not guard against missing auth attribute
findings.explanation: The function assumes conn.auth always exists and has a scopes attribute. If a connection arrives without an auth attribute (e.g., early middleware chain or test harness), a AttributeError will propagate. This is a defensive gap for a library used in varied middleware pipelines.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard to check hasattr(conn, "auth") and that auth has scopes before iterating, returning False (deny access) when auth is absent or malformed.

findings.title: has_required_scope short-circuits on empty scopes list
findings.explanation: When `scopes` is an empty list, the for loop body never executes and the function immediately returns True. This means any connection is treated as having all required scopes when none are specified, which can be an authorization bypass if the caller relies on the function to enforce scope requirements.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit check: if not scopes, return True only when the connection is already authenticated, or document that empty scopes means 'no restriction' and ensure callers handle this case intentionally.
findings.suggested_test: Test that has_required_scope(conn, []) returns True for an authenticated conn, and returns False for an unauthenticated conn when the intent is to require at least one scope.

findings.title: async_wrapper and sync_wrapper do not handle request attribute missing from kwargs
findings.explanation: The wrapper retrieves request from kwargs or positional args via idx, but if neither is present, the assert will raise AssertionError rather than a clear HTTPException or redirect. This can crash the server in edge routing scenarios.
findings.recommendation: Add a None check after request resolution and fall back to a 403/redirect, or ensure the decorator is only applied to routes that always inject a request.

findings.title: requires decorator does not validate scopes type at decorator creation
findings.explanation: If scopes is an empty list or an empty tuple, scopes_list becomes empty, and has_required_scope will always return True (vacuous truth), effectively bypassing authorization. This is not a security flaw per se but a behavioral surprise when callers pass empty scope collections.
findings.recommendation: Add a runtime check that raises ValueError or TypeError when an empty sequence is passed, unless the intent is to allow unrestricted access explicitly documented.

findings.title: AuthCredentials.__init__ mutates the input list when scopes is provided
findings.explanation: While `list(scopes)` creates a shallow copy, the type annotation `typing.Sequence[str] | None` suggests the intent is to accept any sequence. If a caller passes a tuple or other immutable sequence, the code works fine. However, if a mutable list is passed and later code replaces self.scopes, external references to the original list are not affected due to the copy. This is not a bug but worth noting that the copy protection is present.
findings.recommendation: No fix needed; the current implementation correctly copies the input. If the intent is to accept any iterable, consider `list(scopes)` is already there.
findings.suggested_test: Pass a tuple to AuthCredentials and verify self.scopes is a list independent of the original.

findings.title: AuthenticationError exception is defined but never raised in the snapshot
findings.explanation: AuthenticationError is exported but not used anywhere in the visible source. It could be leveraged by custom AuthenticationBackend implementations to signal auth failures explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Consider raising AuthenticationError in AuthenticationBackend.authenticate when appropriate, and document its intended use for downstream backends.
